blocks.text: In 1 Samuel 24, David confronts a defining moment of conscience when opportunity to strike Saul presents itself in the cave at En-gedi. Though his men urge him to act, David refuses, bound by conviction that the LORD's anointed cannot be harmed by his own hand. Even his symbolic cutting of Saul's robe sleeve disturbs him deeply, revealing the strength of his moral restraint. David's refusal grounds itself explicitly in Saul's status as the anointed one—a theological principle that outweighs both personal safety and political advantage. This episode establishes David as someone whose character is defined not by opportunism but by deference to the LORD's choice.
